label: PROMPT EN-1: glibenclamide
title: Glibenclamide for diabetes
statement: In relation to the management of diabetes, the use of oral long-acting sulfonylureas (glibenclamide) should be avoided.

source.document: Cooper JA, et al. The development of the PROMPT criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484, Table 4
source.citation: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484
source.credit: Cooper JA, Ryan C, Smith SM, et al. The development of the PROMPT (PRescribing Optimally in Middle-aged People's Treatments) criteria. BMC Health Serv Res 2014;14:484

plain_summary: Glibenclamide is a long-acting diabetes tablet that can cause low blood sugar that lasts, so safer choices are usually preferred.

medicine_groups.name: Long-acting sulfonylurea, glibenclamide
medicine_groups.note: Gliclazide and glimepiride are not listed because the statement names only glibenclamide.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when glibenclamide is supplied to a person aged 45 to 64 inclusive. If age is missing, record that PROMPT eligibility is unknown. One supply is enough. Other sulfonylureas such as gliclazide are not a finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why it was prescribed, blood glucose and HbA1c results, kidney function, episodes of low blood sugar, and how the person actually takes it.
ask_the_gp: A review of the diabetes treatment, including whether a medicine with less risk of low blood sugar would suit the patient.
